newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees lower foreign debt on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees lower foreign debt on strong dollar.

text.p: Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Wednesday Indonesia's foreign debt was declining due to a weakening of the yen against the U.S. dollar.
"The fall of the yen against the dollar has caused a decline in our foreign debt because about 40 percent of the debts are denominated in yen," he told reporters.
"It depends on who our trade partners are," Mar'ie said when asked if a weaker yen was good for Indonesia's economy.
He said the sharp fall of the yen against the dollar had helped the rupiah appreciate against the yen.
The World Bank estimates Indonesia's foreign debt, including private sector loans, at some $100 billion.
Last Friday, 100 yen was quoted at 1,939 rupiah against 2,120 rupiah a year ago.
